name: Polymarket
summary: Prediction markets’ growing reach, thin take rates, and unresolved ethical and regulatory questions.
overview: Polymarket turns opinions about future events into tradable contracts. The report explores the appeal of those market signals while questioning whether rapid growth in trading activity can become a profitable business at a valuation that already assumes considerable success.

bull_case: A liquid information market could become a useful global forecasting layer.
bear_case: Regulatory uncertainty and event-driven liquidity can limit the addressable market.
latest_round: April 2026: $1B Series E at a reported $15B valuation

intelligence.description: Polymarket operates event-based prediction markets for politics, economics, culture, and other real-world outcomes.
company: Polymarket lets participants trade contracts linked to real-world outcomes, producing market prices that can function as probability signals. The central question is whether prediction-market liquidity can evolve into a broad, durable financial-information business.

Reporting on an April 2026 Series E said Polymarket raised about $1 billion at a $15 billion valuation. ICE's 2025 strategic investment also included a plan to distribute Polymarket's event-driven data.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Polymarket sits at the convergence of retail trading, information markets, crypto infrastructure, and financial-data distribution. Its regulatory path will shape whether prediction markets become a mainstream market-information layer.

changed.text: Polymarket launches as a crypto-native prediction-market platform.
The company raises capital as interest in information markets grows.
Reporting says Polymarket raised about $1 billion in a Series E at a $15 billion valuation.
Regulatory access and repeat use beyond headline events remain the key operating questions.

takeaways: Prediction markets can convert crowd views into continuously updated prices.
Regulatory access is the core constraint on scale.
ICE brings institutional distribution and validation.
Trading volume is not the same as durable revenue.
